newsitem.title: USA: Short-term price costs for Venezuela reforms - Matos.
newsitem.headline: Short-term price costs for Venezuela reforms - Matos.

text.p: Venezuelan Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos said on Monday that there would be some short term inflation costs from labor market and social security reforms, but that this would lead to lower inflation in the longer-term.
"We're going to have inflation today, but we're buying low inflation for the future," Matos told Reuters Financial Television.
He said the four-percent growth target for economic growth for 1997 can be achieved.
"In Venezuela, the real economy is moving," he said.

Matos also said Venezuela intended to have state-owned Banco Republica privatized by August and Banco Latino by July. He said the most difficult privatizations would be the steel and aluminum sectors.
"We are working in a way that I can say today that we have a high probability of getting support from Congress because of the way we have managed the political situation," he said.
He also said he was confident of reaching a standby agreement with the IMF.
